components.html: ISYF 2027
components.css: .ds-plaque { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.625rem; min-height: 48px; padding: 0 1.375rem; border-radius: 2px; background-color: #8e1b1d; color: #f6f5f1; font-family: Lexend, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-plaque:hover { background-color: #6f1416; } .ds-plaque:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #8e1b1d; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-arrow { width: 1.125em; height: 1.125em; transition: transform 250ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-plaque:hover .ds-arrow { transform: translateX(4px); }

components.css: .ds-board { background: #8e1b1d; color: #f6f5f1; padding: 3rem 1.5rem; } .ds-frame { border: 1px solid #e6c878; outline: 1px solid #e6c878; outline-offset: 6px; padding: 2rem; } .ds-board-h { font-family: 'Libre Caslon Display', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: 40px; line-height: 1.1; margin: 0 0 1.5rem; padding-bottom: 1.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid #e6c878; } .ds-roll { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; columns: 2 12rem; column-gap: 3rem; column-rule: 1px solid rgba(230, 200, 120, 0.35); } .ds-roll li { break-inside: avoid; margin-bottom: 1.5rem; } .ds-numeral { display: block; font-family: 'Libre Caslon Display', Georgia, serif; font-size: 28px; line-height: 1; color: #e6c878; margin-bottom: 0.375rem; } .ds-roll a { display: block; color: #f6f5f1; text-decoration: none; padding-block: 0.3rem; } .ds-roll a:hover .ds-name { color: #e6c878; } .ds-roll a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #e6c878; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-name { display: block; font-family: 'Libre Caslon Text', Georgia, serif; font-size: 14px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-field { display: block; font-family: 'Libre Caslon Text', Georgia, serif; font-style: italic; font-size: 14px; color: #f1e0b0; }

narrative.overview:
The ISYF-wide pages (home, history, laureates, the upcoming-edition page) borrow their materials from Hwa Chong Institution's clocktower building: cool plaster-white walls, crimson couplet panels lettered in gilt, and the school's honour boards where names are engraved year by year. The proof ISYF offers is lineage, so the system is built to set records: editions, years, themes and laureate names, ruled and ordered like a ledger rather than dressed up like a summit landing page.

Density is editorial and calm. Plaster carries most of every page; ink hairlines divide it into ruled sections with a heading column; crimson arrives either as small, deliberate marks (years, links, the one primary plaque) or as a whole field (the honour board). Gilt appears only on crimson. Corners are nearly square, nothing floats on shadows, and motion is limited to one settling moment on the honour board and small arrow nudges.
keyCharacteristics: Cool plaster ground, lacquer-ink text, crimson as the single accent
Hairline rules (1px) and double gilt frames instead of cards and shadows
Libre Caslon Display for headings and years; Libre Caslon Text for themes, names and small-caps labels; Lexend for running text
Data-driven lists that grow with each edition

rules.name: The Gilt-on-Crimson Rule
rules.body: Gilt never sits on plaster. It appears on crimson fields, and over darkened photography, and nowhere else.

rules.name: The Mark-or-Field Rule
rules.body: Crimson is either a small mark (a year, a link, one plaque per view) or an entire full-bleed field. No crimson tints as card backgrounds, no crimson side stripes.

rules.name: The Engraved Names Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked serif is reserved for names on the honour board (and the nav's tracked Lexend items). Do not set headings or running text in caps.

rules.name: The Serif Holds the Record Rule
rules.body: Years, themes and names are set in Caslon; explanatory prose is Lexend. Do not swap them.

rules.name: The Frame-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: To set something apart, frame it (1px border plus 1px outline offset 4-6px) or put it on a field. Never lift it on a shadow.

dos: Do scope every heritage rule under `#page.heritage` and re-point shared tokens there; leave `assets/css/index.css` and the `/2026` archive untouched.
Do open each section with a 1px ink rule and separate rows with 1px Hairline Stone.
Do set years, themes and names in Caslon, crimson numerals on plaster and gilt numerals on crimson.
Do use a full crimson field with a double gilt frame when something must stand apart.
Do drive every list and count from `data/` and lay lists out with auto-fill grids or CSS columns so the next committee never hand-tunes layout.
Do keep corners at 2px and tap targets at 44px or more.
donts: Don't use pills, badges, stat boxes, chip clouds, side-stripe cards or shadowed cards.
Don't place a small-caps label above a heading as a kicker; meta lines sit beside or after what they describe.
Don't use icon glyphs or emoji as decoration; the drawn arrow and the social marks are the only icons.
Don't restyle archived edition sites or let heritage styles leak outside `#page.heritage`.
Don't add statistics, testimonials or counts that are not in `data/`.
